Subject: Re: Exploring annual options for inference spend

Mina —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Our finance and cloud teams ran the numbers and we think a multi-year, upfront structure could work if we can align on two things: a) a step-down pricing schedule that matches our adoption profile (small ramp in year 1, material growth in year 2–3), and b) a fair true-up mechanism so we don't overpay during the slow start months.

Attached is a very rough usage estimate for Q4–Q1 and a short doc with our procurement constraints. We're targeting a decision by mid-December. Can Redwood provide a clean proposal that shows: term discount tiers, staged crediting if we miss ramp targets, and any SLA-related concessions for a 3-year commitment?

High level ask: Prefer an upfront prepay for year 1 and 2 (50/50), with year 3 either prepaid or invoiced depending on growth triggers. Open to suggestions.

Best,
Alice

Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask and the estimates — very helpful. We've sketched a structure that tends to work well for customers with slow starts but strong long-term growth. Summary below; I'll attach a single-page term sheet with the numeric examples. Ben (pricing) and Laura (onboarding/ops) are looped in to confirm feasibility.

Proposal summary (high level)
- Term: 3 years.
- Payment cadence: 50% upfront prepay at contract signature (applied across years 1–2 as credit), 25% at start of year 2, 25% at start of year 3 OR opt to true-up monthly against usage if you prefer less upfront in year 3.
- Discounts: 18% on list for 3-year commit vs current usage, stepping down to 12% if we apply quarterly true-ups instead of upfront for year 3.
- Ramp protection: If your realized usage for the first 6 months is < 60% of forecast, we offer a pro-rated credit (up to 20% of year-1 prepay) to be applied to future invoices.
- Stepdown credits: If growth exceeds forecast by >30% in any rolling 6-month window, we automatically allocate extra capacity and discuss an upward true-up at a pre-agreed marginal rate (to avoid surprise overage billing).
- SLAs: Standard Redwood Enterprise SLA applies; for 3yr deals we can provide a 99.9% target for critical routes and a 15% service-credit cap.

Next steps
1) Ben will validate the numeric examples and produce a term sheet (attachment).
2) Laura will outline an onboarding milestone plan with mileposts tied to credits.
3) If that looks good, we'll prepare a clean DocuSign packet for signature and a HubSpot deal update.

I'll attach the draft term sheet — Ben, flagged for any changes.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Quick note with the numbers filled in (see inline). Mina — I refined the ramp protection language slightly to make the credit automatic and time-boxed. Also added a staged true-up cadence for transparency.

Inline highlights from the term sheet
- Notional total list value (est): $2,700,000 over 3 years based on current forecasts.
- 3‑yr commit discount: 18% -> Notional committed spend = $2,214,000.
- Proposed payment schedule: 50% up front = $1,107,000 at signature (applied as a credit across the first 12 months), 25% at Y2 start = $553,500, 25% at Y3 start = $553,500.
- Ramp protection (automatic): If 0–6 month actual usage < 60% of forecast, we issue a credit equal to (forecast - actual)/forecast * 20% of year-1 prepay. Credit applied to Y2 invoice.
- Staged true-up option: Monthly reconciliation with a 30-day notice window; if Finova prefers, we can move to quarterly reconciliations at a reduced discount (12% overall).

Operational notes (Laura):
- Onboarding milestone 1 (1–2 weeks): sandbox access + baseline performance tuning.
- Milestone 2 (month 1): prefix caching configured and initial batch templates in place.
- Milestone 3 (months 2–3): traffic ramp gates, SLA verification, and runbook handoff.

Alice — if you want, we can produce two signature-ready options: (A) maximum discount / maximum prepaid (favored by finance) and (B) staged prepay with monthly true-ups (favored by Cloud Ops). Which do you want to see first?

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter

Team —

Thanks, this is very helpful and much clearer than our initial ask. We discussed internally and want two actionable documents for procurement:

1) Option A: Full upfront (50% at signature, 25% Y2, 25% Y3) with the 18% discount and the automatic ramp-protection credit as written. This is our preferred finance-optimal path.

2) Option B: Staged prepay with monthly reconciliation for Y3, 12% discount, and the same onboarding milestones. Procurement wants the monthly reconciliation spelled out (reporting template + 30-day settlement window).

Please send both as clean PDFs and a short one-page summary we can attach to the PO. If possible, include a line in the term sheet that any unused prepay credit after 36 months can be applied to support costs (not refunded). Procurement asked for that carve-out.

If everything lines up we'll circulate to Legal next week — target signing by 12/20.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Best,
